response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS a FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), b1 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m FROM per_order), s1 AS (SELECT p.a FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN b1 WHERE p.a > b1.m), b2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.a FROM s1 CROSS JOIN b2 WHERE s1.a > b2.m) SELECT AVG(s2.a) AS avg_of_remaining, AVG(s2.a - b1.m) AS avg_excess_over_first, AVG(s2.a - b2.m) AS avg_excess_over_second FROM s2 CROSS JOIN b1 CROSS JOIN b2

assumptions.assumption: Executions with NULL ordersmark are grouped together as a single order (GROUP BY puts NULLs in one group), and that group is included in the first benchmark mean. Orders whose remaincount values are all NULL have a NULL average and are excluded from the mean and the filters.
'Above' means strictly greater than the benchmark.
